dedupe_keys.name: tango of renewables in the triangle of uncertainty a german case study

description: Sandra Franziska Gutjahr, Daniela Thrän and Danial Esmaeili Aliabadi at the Helmholtz Centre for Environmental Research report a German energy-system study using risk-sensitive stochastic optimisation. The model combines historical weather and future climate scenarios to examine variable wind and solar generation with dispatchable bioenergy. The reported outcomes show bioenergy meeting shortages at system costs up to about 10% higher in some conditions, while excessive risk sensitivity can increase fossil-energy dependence. Spatial investment patterns differ across German federal states according to renewable availability. Zenodo supplies the article freely under CC BY 4.0. Coverage is Germany; the metadata do not state all weather years, planning horizons or model-code identity. Related Man0EUvRE bioeconomy outputs are catalogued separately, without asserting that they reproduce this exact experiment. A limitation is that no article body or numerical files were read and the reported findings were not independently reproduced.
